name: SAML federated trust with a tight subject (saml:aud + saml:sub) - does NOT fire the high expansion finding
note: IAM-805 (SAML analogue of the tight-OIDC boundary). A Federated SAML principal with a positive saml:aud audience constraint AND a specific saml:sub subject scopes trust narrowly. A TRUST-FEDERATED relationship is recorded but must NOT reach HIGH.
rationale: For SAML federation, saml:aud is the endpoint URL to which SAML assertions are presented and is a valid audience CONSTRAINT analogous to OIDC aud; a saml:sub bound to one identity narrows the subject. With both present, the trust is scoped to a specific subject rather than an org-wide/absent subject, so the high subject-expansion finding does not apply and severity stays low/medium (trust-policy-semantics 4.5, by analogy to the OIDC test 17 boundary). The analyzer must recognize aud as a constraint (not missing) and must not claim assumption is confirmed - a matching SAML assertion is out of scope. The assumed role's permissions remain out of scope / unknown. Ref: AWS SAML-based federation condition keys (saml:aud); docs/trust-policy-semantics.md sec 4.5.
